title: Delphi After the Oracle
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Nine dated events in Delphi's history after the oracle closed, from the Theodosian Decrees to the UNESCO listing; the learner predicts each event's stage (silenced, found, dug up, shown) before its description is revealed, and each event drops onto a vis-timeline from 300 to 2000 CE with the empty centuries compressed.

educational.topic: Delphi after the oracle: Kastri, rediscovery, the French excavation, and how the site is shown today
learningObjectives: Classify nine events in Delphi's history after the oracle into the four stages silenced, found, dug up, and shown, with at least 8 of 9 correct, predicting each event's stage before its description is revealed.
prerequisites: Theodosian Decrees and the closing of the oracle
Delphic Festivals and the Theater of Delphi

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-reveal classification on a timeline, one prediction per event in date order, with immediate feedback and a compressed time scale
keyQuestions: The oracle fell silent in 391 CE. How did Delphi come back?
What is the difference between finding a site and digging it up?
How much of what visitors see today was shaped after the excavation?
commonMisconceptions: The ruins of Delphi were always visible and visited, when they lay under a village for centuries.
Archaeologists found Delphi by digging, when travelers identified it first from ancient texts.
The excavation was the end of the story, when rebuilding, museums, and festivals shaped what visitors see today.
What we see at Delphi is exactly as the excavators found it, when the Athenian Treasury was rebuilt.
assessmentOpportunities: Prediction score on nine events (mastery: 8 of 9).
Explain why the rebuilt Athenian Treasury belongs to the Shown stage.
